SFH.Settings.SequencesHint: Play the activation and shutdown animation when the projection is raised or lowered.
SFH.Device.OmniHint: Orange hologram projected from a forearm tool
SFH.Device.WristHint: Synthwave screen on a fold-out case
SFH.Settings.WorldDeviceHint: The device players get before they choose one of their own. Your own My device wins over it, unless it is set to Use the world default.
SFH.Settings.DeviceHint: The hardware you are wearing. Each player can choose their own, and it wins over the Default device; choose Use the world default to follow that instead.
SFH.Settings.DeviceOverridden: The Default device is now {world}, but you are still wearing {mine}: your own My device wins over the default. Set My device to Use the world default to follow it.
SFH.Settings.DeckSizeHint: Size of the macro bar keys, in pixels. Lower this if the bar is wider than the device it sits on.
SFH.Settings.GridHint: The fine etching on the Mass Effect and TRON projections: hexes on the omni-tool, a square grid on TRON.
SFH.NoCharacter: No character to project. Assign one to yourself in the player list.
SFH.NoCharacterGM: No character to project. Select a character's or an NPC's token on the canvas.
SFH.NoAdapter: The HUD has no adapter for the {system} system yet, so there is nothing to project.
SFH.ActionFailed: The "{action}" action failed. See the console for details.
SFH.Keybind.HideHint: Clears the device and the projection off the screen without switching them off, so the projection comes back on the same tab. The macro bar stays.
SFH.Hide.Notice: The HUD is hidden. Press {key}, or the eye on the macro bar, to bring it back.
SFH.Hide.NoticeUnbound: The HUD is hidden. Press the eye on the macro bar to bring it back.
SFH.Settings.ControlIconsHint: Gives the scene controls on the left of the screen sci-fi icons — an astronaut for tokens, a radar for measuring, a datapad for notes. Turn it off to keep Foundry's own.
SFH.Settings.ProjScale: Wrist computer and EVA projection size
SFH.Settings.JournalScaleHint: How large the Journal's book opens, as a percentage of the room it could take. At 100 it fills the free space between the panels; lower it to keep more of the map in view. The Grove look follows it too.
SFH.Settings.ProjScaleHint: How much of the free space the Wrist Computer and EVA projections take, as a percentage. Lower it to keep more of the map in view. The Mass Effect omni-tool and TRON are not affected: their projections always match the width of the plate at the foot of the screen, which follows Macro key size.
SFH.Settings.SheetTabs: D&D 5e sheet tabs as a labeled row
SFH.Settings.SheetTabsHint: Lays the tabs of the D&D 5e character, NPC and vehicle sheets in a row across the sheet, each with its name, instead of the icons hung down its side. The rest of the sheet is left as the system draws it. A row too long for its sheet scrolls with the mouse wheel or the arrows at its ends.
SFH.Settings.FontDisplayHint: Your own font for headings, names and panel titles, in place of the device's. Type the font's name as your font list shows it, such as Myriad Pro. A font installed on this computer works, as does one the GM has added under Additional Fonts in Foundry's Core settings, or any Google Fonts family. Add a fallback after a comma. Leave empty for the device's own.
SFH.Settings.FontBodyHint: Your own font for the interface's text — the sidebar, chat, labels and the projection's panels. Type the font's name as your font list shows it, such as Myriad Pro. A font installed on this computer works, as does one the GM has added under Additional Fonts in Foundry's Core settings, or any Google Fonts family. Add a fallback after a comma. Leave empty for the device's own.
SFH.Settings.FontMonoHint: Your own font for numbers and readouts — hit points, modifiers, macro key numbers. A monospaced font keeps columns of numbers lined up. Type the font's name as your font list shows it, such as Myriad Pro. A font installed on this computer works, as does one the GM has added under Additional Fonts in Foundry's Core settings, or any Google Fonts family. Add a fallback after a comma. Leave empty for the device's own.
SFH.Fonts.Missing: The font "{font}" is not installed on this computer, so the HUD is using a stand-in. Install it, have the GM add it under Additional Fonts in Foundry's Core settings, or turn on Fetch fonts from Google Fonts.
SFH.Settings.GoogleFontsHint: When a font named above is not on this computer or in Foundry, fetch it from Google Fonts. Turn it off to keep the table offline. The devices' own fonts ship with the module either way, so they never need fetching.
SFH.Fonts.MissingGoogle: The font "{font}" is not installed on this computer and Google Fonts does not have it, so the HUD is using a stand-in. Install it, or have the GM add it under Additional Fonts in Foundry's Core settings.
SFH.Device.TronHint: Light lines on black, rezzed up from the disc you carry
SFH.Device.VambraceHint: An engraved bracer whose runes kindle and weave the sheet in spell-light
SFH.Device.JournalHint: A leather journal that slides out of its satchel and opens across the table, its writing fading in as you watch
SFH.Device.ReliquaryHint: The Runic Vambrace as a reliquary for a cleric or a paladin: white gold, a rose window of stained glass, and golden light
SFH.Device.RuneforgeHint: The Runic Vambrace forged in stone and brass, its runes glowing like a forge's coals
SFH.Device.WitchfireHint: The Runic Vambrace carved from bone, burning with a green witch-fire
SFH.Device.GroveHint: The Adventurer's Journal as a druid's herbarium, bound in green leather with leaves pressed in its pages
SFH.Device.HoloprojectorHint: The omni-tool as a palm-sized disc emitter, the sheet a flickering blue hologram that wavers into being
SFH.Device.DatapadHint: The wrist computer as a battered handheld datapad, its readout amber on a dark screen
SFH.Device.GauntletHint: The omni-tool as a hammered steel gauntlet with a small red display, its panels gunmetal
SFH.Device.CommHint: The omni-tool as a wrist comm unit in teal and orange, with a hexagonal emitter and cut-cornered panels
SFH.Device.CrystalHint: The Runic Vambrace as a white ceramic band set with a cut crystal, its panels frosted glass
SFH.Device.RetroHint: The EVA console as an old green-phosphor terminal in a beige monitor, typing its panels out as it opens
SFH.Device.CyberdeckHint: TRON's deck as a neon cyberdeck in magenta and cyan, glitching open
SFH.Device.LonestarHint: Fallout 2d20 only, and always worn there: the Pip-Boy's olive forearm unit, whose POWER lamp brings up Scorpious187's Pip-Boy
SFH.Projection.Dossier.LoseHint: Lower the shields by 5, without touching the barrier, armor or hit points
SFH.Projection.Dossier.RegenHint: Recharge the shields by their regeneration, as the start of a turn does
SFH.Projection.Menu.Name: Name
SFH.Projection.NewItemHint: Make a blank item of a kind, and open its sheet to fill it in
SFH.Settings.JournalDark: The Journal's interface in the dark
SFH.Settings.JournalDarkHint: With the Adventurer's Journal or the Grove, draws the sidebar, chat, player list, controls, scene bar and turn order in dark leather with pale ink instead of paper. The journal itself stays paper.
SFH.Settings.ChatCards: Chat cards in the device's colors
SFH.Settings.ChatCardsHint: Draws chat messages and roll results on the device's panels instead of Foundry's parchment. Turn it off if a game system's or module's cards are hard to read this way.
SFH.Settings.CalendariaHint: Draws Calendaria's HUD, calendars and windows in the device's colors and fonts, and follows the device when it changes. Turn it off to use the theme chosen in 3DS:ATLAS's 3DS Themes instead.
SFH.Settings.HeadingColorHint: The color of the headings in the sidebar and the rest of the interface. Leave it empty for the main color of whichever device you are wearing. A color chosen here stays when you change device.
SFH.Settings.CarouselHint: Also shows the turn order as a row of portraits across the top of the screen during an encounter, in your device's style. The tracker in the sidebar stays as it is.
SFH.Settings.CarouselScaleHint: How large the carousel combat tracker is, as a percentage: its portraits, text and controls together.
SFH.Carousel.Target: Target this token. Shift adds it to your targets.
SFH.Settings.CarouselLayoutHint: Where the current turn sits in the carousel. On the left, the row reads as who is up next. Centered, those who just went are on its left and those coming up on its right.
SFH.Settings.SceneBarHint: Shows the scenes as a bar across the top left in your device's style, with a drawer of every scene by folder, a search, and a preview of each scene. Off puts Foundry's own scene list back.
SFH.Settings.SceneBarStartCollapsedHint: Collapses the scene bar each time Foundry loads, whatever it was before.
SFH.Settings.SceneBarCombat: Collapse the scene bar during combat
SFH.Settings.SceneBarCombatHint: Collapses the scene bar while an encounter on your scene is running, and brings it back when the encounter ends. It makes room for the carousel.
SFH.Settings.SceneBarHover: Open the collapsed scene bar on hover
SFH.Settings.SceneBarHoverHint: While the scene bar is collapsed, pointing at it opens it until the pointer leaves.
SFH.Chat.Blind: Blind roll: only the GM sees the result
SFH.Chat.BlindGM: Blind roll: the player cannot see it
SFH.Volume.Hint: What each connected player's own volume sliders are set to, asked from their Foundry: for finding out why someone cannot hear.
SFH.Volume.Locked: No sound until they click on the page
SFH.Volume.NoAnswer: No answer: still loading, or this module is not running for them
SFH.Settings.SceneClick: Clicking a scene in the Scenes tab
SFH.Settings.SceneClickHint: What a click on a scene in the sidebar's Scenes tab does. Shift+click does the other, and the right-click menu still has both.
SFH.Scenes.Label: Scenes
SFH.Scenes.AllHint: Every scene, by folder, with a search
SFH.Scenes.More: {count} more: open them in the drawer
SFH.Scenes.ViewHint: Go there yourself. Clicking a scene does the same.
SFH.Scenes.ActivateHint: Make it the active scene and move everyone there. Double-clicking a scene does the same.
SFH.Scenes.PreloadHint: Load it on every player's machine ahead of time, so switching is quick.
SFH.Scenes.PullHint: Move everyone to this scene without making it active.
SFH.Scenes.InitialHint: Make where you are looking now the scene's starting view.
SFH.Scenes.InitialNotViewed: View this scene first, then set its starting view from where you are looking.
SFH.Scenes.InitialSet: {name}'s starting view is now where you are looking.
SFH.Scenes.NavHint: Show or hide it in the bar, and in players' navigation.
SFH.Scenes.Clash: {module} also replaces the scene navigation. Turn off its scene navigation, or this module's Scene bar setting, so they do not fight over it.
SFH.Settings.SceneBarStyleHint: A bar of the scenes in navigation, or just the Scenes button, which opens every scene by folder with a search and previews. The collapse settings only apply to the bar.
